utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-00-39-PT, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. May I first have the appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, good afternoon, Your Honours, colleagues from the Defence. My name is Mark Harmon. I represent the Prosecutors' office this afternoon. Appearing with me to my right, Mr. Alan Tieger, to his right, Mr. Thomas Hannis. And to my left, Ms. Carmela Annink-Javier, who is the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Harmon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Goran Neskovic, counsel. With me is Deyan Brashich.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neskovic. Before we start, I would like to hear from the Defence who is this afternoon representing the defendant. Is it you, Mr. Neskovic, as co-counsel, or Mr. Brashich?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am appearing here only as a temporary legal consultant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What about your duties under the rules? I mean, if you are withdrawn, you are not supposed to --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have been withdrawn as lead counsel, that does not immediately end your duties as counsel. Isn't that true? Have you oriented yourself to what your duties are at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honour. And there is a decision dated May 2nd, 2003, by the Registrar which outlines my continuing duties to transfer the case to a lead counsel and to facilitate such transfer, which I'm fully prepared to do. I do not believe that I can speak on behalf of Mr. Krajisnik. My role, I think, is limited by that May 2nd order of the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are withdrawn as lead counsel. At the same time, Article 20 of the -- are you aware of what Article 20 of the directive of assignment of Defence counsel instructs you to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I have read it, Your Honour, but as I stand here and now, I cannot repeat it verbatim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What would it be, not verbatim? What would be your duty if --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: It would be my duty to assist in the transfer of materials, work product, and aid the incoming counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Article 20 says that "when the assignment of counsel is withdrawn, that counsel assigned may not withdraw from acting until either a replacement counsel has been provided by the tribunal or by the suspect or the accused or the suspect or accused has declared his intention in writing to conduct his own Defence." And paragraph (b) reads that "the withdrawn counsel may in the interests of justice, may continue to represent the suspects or the accused for a period of not exceeding 30 days after the date on which the replacement is assigned." So it's not -- but I do understand that you've chosen that Mr. Neskovic today will act as counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: The reason I have done so, Your Honour, is that there might be an appearance that I would be acting in conflict of a court of competent jurisdiction. It is for that reason that that matter will be cleared up on the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Should this Court, however, order me on the transcript to continue representing the interests of Mr. Krajisnik, I'm fully -- for this period of 30 days, I am fully prepared to do so if this Court will so order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you, but I'm just trying to find out whether the Defence has taken its decision in full knowledge of the applicable law in this respect. Mr. Neskovic, I have been informed that Mr. Krajisnik would prefer this Status Conference to be in closed session. Is that correct information?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. Mr. Krajisnik just informed me about this a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You know that usually, the public character of our hearings is considered to be of great importance. Could you or could Mr. Krajisnik give us the specific reasons why he would prefer to have this matter - we don't even know what the matter is - but whether the matter should be dealt with in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krajisnik has asked to take the floor and explain why he wishes a closed session, after which he would explain his opinion to Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think private session would do, but I'm looking to you, Madam Registrar. Private session means that we are not pulling down all the curtains, but that whatever Mr. Krajisnik tells us will not be made known to the public. We'll then turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are in open session again. Before we start discussing the substance of what is on our desk, I'd first like since you see new faces on the Bench, I'd first like to introduce to the Defence and to the Prosecution, to you, Mr. Krajisnik, the Judges. This is the first Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. time that this Chamber is sitting in the composition as it is assigned to hear your case. That means, to the left of me is Judge Martin Canivell who has been recently appointed and recently assigned to the case. And to my right is Judge El Mahdi. I think I introduced myself already in the previous hearing. My name is Judge Orie, and I'll preside the case. Let's first spend a moment on the reason why we have a Status Conference because there was a Pre-Trial Conference scheduled for Friday, the 9th of May. It had to be cancelled, just as the commencement of the trial which was scheduled for the 12th of May also had to be cancelled. Reason for cancelling both the Pre-Trial Conference and the commencement of the trial is the unavailability of lead counsel, Mr. Brashich. And the reason of his unavailability is that Mr. Brashich was by disciplinary decision suspended to practice by a court in New York. That therefore, he could not continue to act as counsel before this Tribunal. This has become known only recently within the Tribunal; and therefore, we were a bit surprised by it. The reason why you, Mr. Brashich, cannot continue to act as lead counsel is that you do not fulfill the requirements any more, the requirements of Article 14 of the directive on the assignment of counsel. The Registrar is under Rule 19(C) under an obligation to withdraw your assignment. That reads the Registrar shall withdraw, not may, but shall withdraw the assignment of counsel where counsel no longer satisfies the requirements of Article 14 (A), and the requirements of Article 14 (A) are that the counsel is admitted to the practice of a law in a state and that he has not been found guilty in relevant disciplinary proceedings against him where he is admitted to the practice of law. So that has changed. We'll not spend much time on it, but may I ask you, Mr. Brashich, when was this decision taken that you were suspended?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: It was taken as of April 1. I received it on April 6th. I notified the Court, this Tribunal, on the 10th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you send it by telefax or --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I sent it both by telefax, and I thought without enclosures. I then Federal Expressed the same letter, and each and every relevant decision, some of which made recommendations that the proceedings against me be dismissed, and another decision that recommended that I be reprimanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Neskovic, when did you become aware of this situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I became aware of that situation on the 29th of April when I was informed by Mr. Brashich about this in a telephone conversation, except that that decision hadn't come into force because Mr. Brashich appealed that decision. But officially, it was only last week - I can't tell you the exact date - but that's when I was officially informed that Mr. Brashich had been suspended. And I found out about this Status Conference on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Brashich, why didn't you send a copy of the letter that you sent to many people to co-counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I have no answer for that, Your Honour. I made a copy of it available to Mr. Kostic the same day that I made the letter available to the Tribunal. I also sent a copy of the letter and enclosures, to my client, again by Federal Express --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have listed on the bottom of your letter to whom you sent copies. But my question was --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Frankly, I was taken aback when I received the order. I did not expect it. And if I had not sent it to Mr. Neskovic, that was my fault, and it was an oversight on my part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your answer, Mr. Brashich. Mr. Neskovic, do I understand well that you're supposed to not be present during the trial? Is that what you expected?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in fact, in an agreement that we had among the Defence, what we had planned was that I would be a man in the field because I was appointed as a co-counsel two months ago. And before that, I was a legal advisor. And I exclusively worked on the matters preparing the Defence so there would be that stage of the trial when the Defence would present its case. As far as the initial stage when the Prosecution is presenting its case, I did not deal with these matters, partly because I did not have the documents. And according to our internal agreement, it was Mr. Brashich and Mr. Kostic who received these documents, and they prepared the concept. But my task, according to the instructions I received from the lawyers, is that in the field, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, I would be gathering evidence we would be needing when the Defence starts presenting its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. You said the agreement. Was this a written agreement between you or has it been put down in correspondence, or was it just an oral agreement on who would do what?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was a verbal agreement among us. And of course, we agreed with our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. It's a very complex case, Your Honour, and it's not just a small local case. This is a case involving 34 municipalities. That is an entire state. It goes from command responsibility of the army to police, legal authorities. So really, one man has to coordinate all this work in the field so that we can achieve maximum effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, I want to stress that you are not responsible for the conduct of lead counsel in this case. I hope that you'll accept from me that we are here to see how we can solve the problems, the problems that you are confronted with, but for which you are not to be blamed because it's not your fault, it's not your mistake. But nevertheless, you're confronted with the consequences of it. It seems that the Defence has to be reorganised one way or the other. And that's the main reason why we're here, first to establish what the reason is that your trial couldn't start, and now to see how we can solve the problems in order that your trial will start as soon as possible. I have a few questions. You don't have to stand up all the time, because if I would speak longer to you, then please sit down if you prefer to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first ask whether any of the other members of the Defence team, as it was constituted until now, has any similar problems? Mr. Neskovic, have you ever had any disciplinary problems in your own system or are you currently facing any similar problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Never, I have never had any disciplinary proceedings issued against me, not just within a bar association or any time in my life. This is a problem which has obviously surprised me as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course I'm not suggesting that you ever had, but you may understand that the Tribunal might be a bit more concerned about disciplinary proceedings in the past or even in the present. Mr. Brashich, are you aware of any similar problems as far as Mr. Kostic is concerned, who...?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I have spoken to Mr. Kostic when this came out, and I don't believe that he has ever had any admonition, censure, or anything similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ask him specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I spoke to him quite extensively about it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Neskovic has something to add, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About half an hour ago, I spoke to Mr. Kostic. He phoned me in my office. He apologised for not being present at this Status Conference. It's because a relative of his was seriously ill. And he said that he was prepared to continue working here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Neskovic, to what extent would you please available to continue to work either here in The Hague or in the field, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be frank, I would be more prepared, more willing to work in the field, for two reasons: First of all, I'm very well acquainted with the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I know the people there. I know what the possibilities are for finding evidence. But given that I'm not familiar with the Anglo-Saxon system, it might be more difficult for me to be present here. Up until now, I have been gathering this evidence, but someone who knows the Anglo-Saxon system would know when, how, and in what manner to use such evidence. But I by no means refuse to work in this Tribunal, nor do I refuse to work for Mr. Krajisnik as I have been working for him for three years now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you be available, let's say, temporarily to act as counsel here in The Hague? That means, for example, if you say I prefer to work in the field, that until a new lead counsel has been assigned, that you would be available, well, let's say, up until August? Would that be something you would consider?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's difficult for me to express a position on that matter right now. It depends on the phase of the proceedings in August. You know, if it's a matter of cross-examining witnesses, that would be a little more difficult, and I don't have the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. documents, nor do I have the conception of this case that Mr. Brashich has. So I ought to think about this before I inform the Trial Chamber of my decision. It's a rather sudden matter for me. I'm slightly surprised by this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you include in your consideration as well that Mr. Brashich has been assigned as consultant in order to make available his knowledge of the case to whomever would succeed him. Mr. Krajisnik, I noticed that you'd like to say something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to be of assistance, if I may, to assist you so that you can assist me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wouldn't want Mr. Kostic or Mr. Neskovic to take over this case at this moment because I don't know how familiar they are with this case. And this is why I'm asking you, the Registrar, has made it possible for all the members of the Defence team apart from Mr. Kostic for them to be with me tomorrow. And then after we have discussed this, I'd be glad to have one of them as lead counsel. But at the moment, I'm prepared to take a decision to find a new lawyer. I was thinking of it -- I thought that this lawyer could be someone like Mr. Brashich. I'm sorry if I'm speaking openly about this matter, but at the moment I have to speak openly about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's no problem. It's not my suggestion that you had invited to give your final view by today because I do understand that it needs more for you to make up your mind as to what direction we would go. But I'm just trying to find out what would be possibilities and opportunities as far as the availability is concerned of the present members of your Defence team. As far as the -- well, the matter of being acquainted with the case is concerned, the only thing I could tell you is that Mr. Kostic until now spent approximately 2.400 hours on the case, so one would expect him to know something about the case. And as far as Mr. Neskovic is concerned, that would be 4.683 hours. So one would also expect that he at least has a global knowledge of what the case is about. My next question would be to you, Mr. Neskovic, or to you,

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: You have recently spoken with Mr. Kostic. What would be his availability?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Your Honour, we were prepared to try this case, as Mr. Neskovic had stated, we had divided the responsibilities of the Defence. Mr. Neskovic was -- his roll was to in the pre-trial stage prepare for the actual Defence, and also in the pre-trial stage to help with regard to meeting some of the issues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was whether Mr. Kostic was available.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: He was available, Your Honour, as I had said, that we would divide the labour on the Prosecution's case between himself and myself, on that understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that unchanged? I mean, of course, the situation has changed, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: With regard to myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But would Mr. Kostic be available to come and to hear the opening statement of the Prosecution, and then start cross-examining witnesses for the Prosecution? It's a very practical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I believe that he would be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On from when?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I believe we had an informal meeting. There was -- I believe the term that Mr. Kostic used last week was that he would need somewhat of some breathing room, and I'm putting that in quotes, and somewhere in the beginning or middle of June. I believe that was the statement that he made at that particular meeting to which I'm sure that Your Honour remembers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I think he stands by that commitment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would that then be an availability that would be temporary or would that be for the rest of the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honour, that would be for the rest of the trial. The only caveat that I would have to point out, that he had wanted some input and assistance from me because most of the preparation that I had done is, unfortunately, locked in my brain, and I can't download the knowledge that I have into his brain as from one computer hard drive to another. That's the only caveat that I recall him making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that is, may I say, a conditional availability.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: It's availability with that one caveat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Another issue that might be of some relevance is that the registry has given recently as far as I understand information as to the financial aspects of the Defence in this case. Would that cause any reluctance to act as counsel as far as you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: That is a matter of hot debate, Your Honour, which is ongoing. I have not caucused with other members of the association. We had a meeting on that issue with the registry last Thursday. I thereafter spoke to Mr. Krajisnik and apprised him of the new regime. And that matter is still up in the air. And after meeting with Mr. Krajisnik, Mr. Kostic relayed to the senior legal officer, Mr. Harhoff, his views on the resources issue, and I believe that is a memorandum dated the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that matter should have been settled also before we would know whether Mr. Kostic would be available.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: There was a meeting which took place with the registry and the executive -- at least one or two members of the executive council of the association on Thursday -- I'm sorry, on Friday evening at 5.00. There was a letter circulated to the membership of the association by email. And I believe that the association is going to take a position on that matter either today or tomorrow. I have not been apprised as to exactly what action it's going to take. Mr. Krajisnik voiced the opinion, which Mr. Kostic transmitted to Mr. Harhoff, that under the new regime, he would -- the Defence team could not be constituted in a fashion or to a level that Mr. Krajisnik feels his Defence should be afforded. The registry has taken the position that the regime is the regime. And I believe that Mr. Kostic, with a change of the present regime, not in dollars and cents, but in the method of payment, would be willing to accept the role throughout the term that the trial is expected to last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that there's no full agreement yet. Do you have any idea on what has been spent on the Defence just -- not costs, not travel expenses, et cetera, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I would estimate, Your Honour, and I haven't seen any hard figures, but on a case of this magnitude, which has now lasted over three years, when you have a number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Somewhere around 900.000 dollars to a million dollars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, add 50 per cent, and you might be closer to the outcome. Do you know how many hours have been spent on preparing this case, all-included, counsel, consultants, investigators?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I would say with the Prosecution, probably somewhere -- if both sides are considered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: You asked me how many hours had been spent, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on the preparation of the Defence and at this moment the problems are -- have arisen in the Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would probably estimate that including investigators, all-told in hours, between 15 and 20.000 hours for the 36 municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There, again, according to my information, you could add 50 per cent to that figure in order to come closer to what the actual figure is. You'll understand that the Tribunal might have some concern about how time and money is spent in preparing the Defence case, that after such a long period of time, that the -- that there are difficulties to commence with the trial, apart from the causes of these difficulties. But there has been a considerable amount of money involved, a considerable number of hours involved, and nevertheless, we are not in a position to start. Mr. Krajisnik, I again emphasise that this is not your fault, not your -- you're not to be blamed for that. And since I also do understand that you might not be fully aware of what actually this system is, since in the correspondence, it appears that there might be some misunderstandings now and then, I'd like to explain to you in relative detail what exactly this system of assignment of counsel includes. So if you would please listen to that. First of all, the Statute in Article 21, paragraph 4 under (d) entitles you to defend yourself in person or through legal assistance of your own choosing, to be informed if you have not legal assistance of this right to be assisted by counsel, and to have legal assistance assigned to the accused in any case where the interests of justice are required, and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it. So that's Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the basic rule. Then, in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, Rule 45, reference is made to the directive on the assignment of Defence counsel. Article 45, under (c) -- no, I am making a mistake. Article 45, under (a) says that "whenever the interests of justice so demands, counsel shall be assigned to suspects or accused who lack the means to remunerate such counsel." And reference is made to the directive on the assignment of Defence counsel. In this directive, you find further rules as to the assignment of counsel. Paragraph 6 deals with the right to assign counsel. There again it's repeated in 6 (a) that "suspects or accused who lack the means to remunerate counsel shall be entitled to assignment of counsel paid for by the Tribunal." It also says, under 6 (c), that "for suspects or accused who dispose of means to partially remunerate counsel, the Tribunal shall pay that portion which the suspect or accused does not have sufficient means to pay for." A decision on the assignment of counsel is given by the Registrar. In Article 11, it reads that the Registrar, after having examined the declaration of means and relevant information obtained, the Registrar shall determine how far the suspect or accused lacks the means to remunerate counsel and shall decide to assign counsel and choose for this purpose a name from the list drawn up in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. So the registry will assign counsel and choose a name from a list of counsel that are available. But there is a possibility also to have counsel assigned whose name do not appear on the list in exceptional circumstances. Although it seems that again such a decision of the Registrar, a decision to assign counsel or to decide that you should partially pay for Defence counsel assigned to you, it seems that under Rule 13 (b), that there's no remedy against it. But if we look at Rule 18 (a) and (c), it seems that a remedy, that means a review by the President of the Tribunal would be available. At least, the Rules are not perfectly clear in this respect, but I would say if you would not be -- if you would have difficulties to accept such a decision, that at least under some circumstances, there is a remedy, and you can ask for review of the decision by the President. There does exist case law in this Tribunal which indicates that the Registrar is under an obligation to consult you before counsel will be assigned. There are several decisions, some suggesting that the Registrar should follow your preference unless there are good reasons not to do so; other decisions suggesting that the Registrar is not under an obligation to follow your preference, but at least should give it full consideration whether the Registrar should not follow your preference. I do understand that you're not going to express yourself on your preference since you have not talked to the members of your Defence team at this very moment. But nevertheless, I think it's of importance to look at the present situation and to see what as a matter of fact the options are. But since this is not primarily the responsibility of the Chamber, but of the registry, I would like to invite the registry to tell this Chamber what, in the view of the registry, would be the options in the present situation for you, reorganising your Defence team. I invited a representative of the registry, Mr. Pimentel. Could you inform the Court on what in view of you would be the options available at this very moment, keeping in mind that the Chamber very much would like to start the trial as soon as possible. And that's in accordance with what Mr. Krajisnik would like to happen. Would you inform the Chamber about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PIMENTEL
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of the Registrar who could not be here himself. I am appearing, I am David Pimentel, the chief of court of management in the registry. Responding to your question, in order to start the trial as soon as Your Honour has expressed that the desire of the Chamber, there are relatively few options, given the amount of preparation necessary to proceed. The options as we see it are as follows: One would be to appoint Mr. Kostic as lead counsel. The amount of time he has invested in preparation of the case should prepare him adequately to assume a competent role as lead counsel. Another option would be to assign Mr. Neskovic or Mr. Kostic on a temporary basis to assume the role of lead counsel while new counsel is appointed and prepares to take over on an ongoing basis. The thought would be that that may be a period of two or three months while new counsel gets up to speed and is in a position to take over the case as lead counsel. Another option that may be more difficult to implement but may still be a possibility would be to bring in someone on a temporary basis, someone else from outside the current Defence team, to assist -- to play the role of lead counsel assisted by Mr. Neskovic and Mr. Brashich. I might add that under all of these scenarios, it's essential that Mr. Brashich be retained as a legal consultant so that his knowledge of the case would be available to whoever served in the lead counsel role. Those, we see, as the essential options if the trial is to start soon. If none of these options are available, either because the attorneys involved are not willing to proceed under those circumstances, or if it's determined that the Chamber will defer to Mr. Krajisnik's preferences and he does not choose to go with one of these options, we see no way to proceed with the case on a short-term basis. We believe it will be necessary to delay the start of the trial for a period of at least two to three months while new lead counsel is appointed and prepares to take responsibility for the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that would bring us close to the summer recess, which would then perhaps mean that we could start only in September. Is that -- SPEAKER: As a practical matter, that would be the logical way to approach it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Pimentel for informing the Chamber. I would like to turn into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We all are aware of the difficult circumstances we're in. Mr. Krajisnik, you'd like the trial to start as soon as possible. That's also what the Tribunal would like to happen. At the same time, you are aware that you have to make up your mind. That's the reason why I asked the registry what the options would be in their view. You've heard them all, Mr. Kostic being assigned as lead counsel. And of course, we would have to solve a few problems there as well, which I just pointed at in my conversation with Mr. Brashich. There would be other solutions. They have all been explained to you by the Defence. I'd like to stress again what the system is. The system is that your preference should be taken into serious consideration. As you might be aware of, that your preference until now of Mr. Brashich has resulted in -- well, I would say this disastrous situation that we are in at this very moment. But nevertheless, your preference, you should be consulted on the preference -- I do understand that you will meet with all available members of the Defence team soon, and I suggest to the registry that in view of the Chamber, it would be fair to receive your view, well, let's say, within approximately one week choosing of these options. If you would consider also, and I noticed that you have done so before, if you would consider also to ask for assignment of someone who's not yet familiar with the case, and I can tell you that upon all your suggestions, the registry has taken the necessary steps in order to see whether counsel you mentioned were available or not. But if you would consider to be assisted by counsel that are not part of your Defence team at this very moment, that you, of course, could give your suggestions to that solution as well whether it would be a temporary assignment, for example, I would consider that the registry -- one of the options of the registry was that, for example, Mr. Neskovic would assist a temporary but experienced Defence counsel who would just assist you in the first stages of the trial, and perhaps the counsel to be assigned on longer term making himself acquainted with the case meanwhile. That's one of the options. So that would require an outside counsel, counsel not yet known to you to be assigned. If you're thinking of this, also discuss the matter with the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. registry. They know perhaps Defence counsel. They might inform you about available Defence counsel, and then you could consider whether this would be a solution. May I ask the representative of the registry also whether they would be willing to assist Mr. Krajisnik if he would consider to have counsel not yet known to him assigned to his team, whether they could give him relevant information as to experienced and available Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. PIMENTEL
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. We maintain a list of counsel who have expressed interest and the association for Defence counsel has verified the qualifications of a number of individuals. We can make those names available to Mr. Krajisnik, and he may make a selection from that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could that be done in short term? I mean, I suggest to you that in order to assign new lead counsel, or at least to find a solution, a way out of this very embarrassing situation, that Mr. Krajisnik should have some time to consider his position, to speak to the available members of the present Defence team, and also to consult you on any outsider who could join the team. Mr. Krajisnik, how much time if the registry would give you proper information and if you would have an opportunity to speak with the present members of the team, how much time do you think you would need in order to express preference as to the kind of solution to be found?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the only thing I would like to ask is because we have three days during which I'm to meet my Defence, I would like to meet also with Mr. Brashich. I don't know why the possibility has not been given to him to be present at this meeting. I hope that next week, after I look at the whole situation, then I would be able to make a decision. I'd like to have a lead counsel as soon as possible so that the trial can start. But I would like to speak to him as soon as possible, Your Honours, if you'll allow me just for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at this very moment, you'd like to speak with Mr. Brashich. No? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to follow you. The perhaps I do not understand exactly what you said. The transcript reads: "I would like to meet also with Mr. Brashich. I don't know why the possibility has not been given to him at this meeting."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here is the situation. I have been approved by the registry to have a meeting with the Defence team, tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow. And on that list, Mr. Brashich is not present. This is to have consultations regarding the case and these outstanding matters. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you'd like to meet with members of the Defence team including the present consultant, Mr. Brashich.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The message at least is clear. It is not this Chamber who decides on who you are allowed to meet with, but your wish at least is very clear. And then you'd say in approximately one week you'd make up your mind as to what solution to find?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. But that's -- I'll give you the reason why I've mentioned Mr. Brashich, because I believe this is relevant for today, because Mr. Brashich has his case to be heard in New York, and there are certain obstacles for him to be present at the meeting. Now, if the Trial Chamber would give an order, then that would be sorted. He would be able to attend this meeting with me and the other members of the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Brashich, could you give any information as to your availability for discussions with Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I had advised Chambers, my attorneys were contacted by the clerk of court of the appellate division with a request that the motion for reconsideration and modification be made. Before I came to The Hague, my attorneys filed that motion. I have to be in New York on the 15th at 9.00 so as to also be able to clarify should that motion not be granted the scope of what I can and cannot do to help Mr. Krajisnik. I cannot adjourn the May 15th date because every time that that is adjourned, the scope of my engagement for Mr. Krajisnik is delayed. My attorneys have cautioned me that I should not in any way give counsel or otherwise appear to act as an attorney until this matter is clarified. The order of suspension is for one year. I do not want to find myself at the end of 11 months from now in a position where my reinstatement has been jeopardised by any actions that I have taken which might have gone, if not against the letter, but then the intent, or vice versa, of the order of suspension, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that it's in your interest to keep at a distance, and at the same time, it's quite clear that Mr. Krajisnik says that he needs you at this very moment. Would you be available for consultation tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I have a flight 11.15, Your Honour. I would be available between 8.00 and 9.30, whatever it takes to get to the airport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I hate to put another burden on the travel office, which is overburdened, but as I had stated to the senior legal officer, I'm fully prepared to do everything in my power to assist Mr. Krajisnik and his confidence in me so that the problem that I have caused would have as little impact on him and on this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you again be available on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Friday is the 15th, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I can possibly take a late flight tomorrow, to be able to get me in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Would you please explore whatever possibilities there are together with Mr. Krajisnik and the registry. I'm not fully aware of the times with which you can meet with your client. I do not know when the other members of the team are available. But would you do the utmost possible --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, may I consult with Mr. Neskovic for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic advises me that they're arriving tomorrow, and that he has a scheduled meeting at 1.00. Your Honour, I'll make a representation that I will make every effort to be at that meeting for whatever period of time. But I am conditioning that upon my consultation with John Walsh and his associates who are acting as my counsel in New York. And I would have to follow their advice as to the attendance at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which is quite apart from -- the views of Mr. Walsh are not necessarily in accordance with what the Tribunal would expect you to do. But since we do not know that view, I would just indicate to you that however important such advice may be for you, but it's finally your own responsibility what you'll do and what you'll not do. I think we have discussed at this very moment whatever has to be discussed. I live in the expectation that having listened well to you, Mr. Krajisnik as well, that this Chamber could expect that a constructive solution could be worked on approximately one week from now on when you have made up your mind. I also hope that it's entirely clear to you that where the registry is under an obligation to consult you and where your preference is of importance for the decision of the registry, it might not be the final word on who will be assigned because your right to be assisted by counsel of your own choosing, even if you cannot afford to pay for it by yourself or partially to pay for it by yourself, is not an absolute right, but find its limits somewhere. And we might have come close to those limits if no workable solution is found on very short notice.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say something. I just wanted to ask you if I can have until the end of next week to decide, because I have a meeting, and then there is a weekend, all that. So if I can have time until the end of next week regarding my decision with relation to the lead counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I'm not granting you the time. The only thing I'm indicating is that the sooner you come up with a suggestion that could be followed or would be acceptable for the registry, the sooner they might give a decision. And whether a week would be reasonable or six days or eight days, that's not up for this Chamber to decide. But you may be aware that the Chamber is very much concerned about the present situation not created by yourself, but nevertheless existing, and a solution has to be found as soon as possible. And the sooner you come up with your own views and your own preferences, the better the chance that they can taken into due consideration. Yes? Is there anything else one of the parties would like to raise at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There's nothing on behalf of the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Neskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, it's common that at Status Conferences, we always try to get proper information about your health situation. It's not a long time ago that we had our last conference. So if there would be any changes, the Chamber would like to be informed about it; and then if you would prefer to do so, we could do it in private session as well. If there have been no changes, then we can conclude this Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I feel great, so there are no problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This then concludes this Status Conference. I indicate that even if a decision would be taken on short notice, that the Prosecution would need at least until the 2nd of June to prepare for -- but that would be, I take it, on the assumption that a decision would be taken by now. So if they would need approximately two and a half weeks for preparation for the witnesses to appear, that whenever the decision will be delayed, the start of the trial would be delayed accordingly. Is that a correct understanding, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's my understanding after checking with the witness unit that from the date of the decision, it would be approximately two weeks for arrangements to be made for witnesses to start appearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that would prevent a start on very short notice anyhow. But the Chamber still would very much prefer to start before the summer recess, and well in advance of the summer recess, because it's of no use to start on the 29th of July and go into recess on the 2nd of August, or whatever date it will be. So I expect everyone, but I'm especially looking to the Defence, and to you, Mr. Krajisnik, to do whatever is possible to resolve the matter and enable the trial to start as soon as possible. The Chamber adjourns.
